questions.question: What happens to the badge on a session card that has **five or more** high-risk items?

options.text: It shows a prominent red badge to shout for triage attention
It stays in the same subdued, muted style as lower counts with no loud red wash

questions.explanation: The update removed the loud red warning at five or more — all high-risk counts now use the quieter muted badge appearance.

questions.question: What does the **finished screen** now show at the top when a session ends?
evidenceFactIds: b: Before state - finished screen only showed custom summary and skipped list
a: General outside knowledge - scores/judgment which card says is explicitly avoided

options.text: A scored judgment with points for how many changes you covered
Only the custom summary text and a list of skipped items with no overall count
A one-line totals sentence stating how many changes were in the session, how many you skipped, and how many you never opened

distractorSources: b: Before state - finished screen only showed custom summary and skipped list
a: General outside knowledge - scores/judgment which card says is explicitly avoided
questions.explanation: The change adds a plain totals sentence like "This session had 12 changes — you skipped 3 and never opened 2" to give a clear wrap-up without scores or judgment.

questions.question: After you finish a session in the **reader**, what does the **wrap-up** screen now show?
evidenceFactIds: Before: wrap-up only knew general summary and skipped items
Before: no count for never-opened changes

options.text: Only the general summary and which items were skipped, with no counts
A totals sentence with the **total** number of changes and the **never-opened** count
Only the count of changes you opened, hiding the total

distractorSources: Before: wrap-up only knew general summary and skipped items
Before: no count for never-opened changes
questions.explanation: The reader now tallies every change with no progress as **never opened** and passes the **total** plus that count to the wrap-up to render a plain summary line.

questions.question: What now appears in the **end-of-session summary** on the Review showcase page?
evidenceFactIds: Before: Review showcase rendered end summaries without numeric totals, so the overall counts were not visible on the page.

options.text: It shows end summaries without numeric totals, so overall counts are not visible
It shows both the total number of changes and how many were never opened as a verifiable sentence

distractorSources: Before: Review showcase rendered end summaries without numeric totals, so the overall counts were not visible on the page.
questions.explanation: The page now passes explicit total and neverOpened numbers to the summary, so both example summaries display a checkable totals sentence.
